title: A Simplified, Langendorff-Free Method for Concomitant Isolation of Viable Cardiac Myocytes and Nonmyocytes From the Adult Mouse Heart
markdown:
## Protocol: Langendorff-free isolation and calcium-tolerant culture of adult mouse cardiomyocytes

### Overview

This protocol outlines a Langendorff-free method for isolating adult mouse cardiomyocytes (CMs) and maintaining them in calcium-tolerant culture. The process involves heart extraction, enzymatic digestion via sequential buffer injections, tissue dissociation, filtration, and gravity-based settling to enrich myocytes while gradually restoring physiological calcium levels. Isolated CMs can be plated on laminin-coated surfaces for subsequent culture.

### Materials/Reagents

EDTA buffer, perfusion buffer, collagenase buffer, stop buffer, intermediate calcium reintroduction buffers, plating media, culture media, laminin (5 μg/mL), sterile 10 mL syringes, sterile 27 G hypodermic needles, Reynolds forceps, 60-mm dish, 100-μm filter, hemocytometer, tissue culture plastic or glass coverslips.

### Equipment

Anesthesia equipment, chest opening tools, syringes with attached needles, forceps, dishes, filters, incubator (37°C, 5% CO2, humidified).

### Safety & Sterility

All buffers and media were prepared as detailed in [Appendix D]. Sterile 10 mL syringes and sterile 27 G hypodermic needles were used for buffer apportionment. Tissue culture was performed in a humidified incubator at 37°C with 5% CO2.

## Reagent Preparation

### Preparation

1. Prepare buffers and media as detailed in [Appendix D]. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S01 -->
2. Apportion EDTA, perfusion, and collagenase buffers into sterile 10 mL syringes, and attach sterile 27 G hypodermic needles ([Online Figure IA]). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S02 -->

## Cardiac Myocyte Isolation

### Heart Extraction and Preclearing

1. Anesthetize C57/BL6J mice aged 8 to 12 weeks, and open the chest to expose the heart. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S01 -->
2. Cut the descending aorta, and immediately flush the heart by injecting 7 mL of EDTA buffer into the right ventricle. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S02 -->
3. Clamp the ascending aorta using Reynolds forceps, and transfer the heart to a 60-mm dish containing fresh EDTA buffer. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S03 -->

### Digestion

1. Achieve digestion by sequentially injecting 10 mL of EDTA buffer, 3 mL of perfusion buffer, and 30 to 50 mL of collagenase buffer into the left ventricle (LV). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S01 -->

### Tissue Dissociation

1. Separate the constituent chambers (atria, LV, and right ventricle), and gently pull them into 1-mm pieces using forceps. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S01 -->
2. Complete cellular dissociation by gentle trituration. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S02 -->
3. Inhibit enzyme activity by adding 5 mL of stop buffer. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S03 -->

### Filtration and Gravity Settling

1. Pass the cell suspension through a 100-μm filter. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S01 -->
2. Subject cells to 4 sequential rounds of gravity settling, using 3 intermediate calcium reintroduction buffers to gradually restore calcium concentration to physiological levels. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S02 -->
3. Collect the cell pellet from each round, which is enriched with myocytes and ultimately forms a highly pure myocyte fraction. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S03 -->
4. Combine the supernatant from each round to produce a fraction containing nonmyocyte cardiac populations. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S04 -->

### Quantification

1. Quantify CM yields and the percentage of viable rod-shaped cells using a hemocytometer. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S01 -->

### CM Culture

#### Branch A: CM Plating

1. Where required, resuspend CMs in prewarmed plating media and plate them at an application-dependent density onto laminin (5 μg/mL) precoated tissue culture plastic or glass coverslips, in a humidified tissue culture incubator (37°C, 5% CO2). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T5-S01 -->

#### Branch A: CM Maintenance

1. After 1 hour, and every 48 hours thereafter, change the media to fresh, prewarmed culture media. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T5-S02 -->
